title: dynasm.lua emits #line directives with unescaped Windows backslash paths, breaking any checkout whose absolute path contains an invalid C escape sequence
symptom: On Windows, `zig build test-lua` fails while compiling the host buildvm tool with dozens of errors of the form "unknown escape sequence '\c'" / "unknown escape sequence '\s'" / "\U used with no following hex digits", all pointing at #line directives inside the generated .zig-cache/o/<hash>/buildvm_arch.h. Observed as 77 compilation errors. Whether a given machine is affected depends entirely on the letters that happen to follow the backslashes in the repository's own absolute path.
root_cause: vendor/luajit/dynasm/dynasm.lua line 88 emits a C #line directive by string-concatenating the input filename directly into a C string literal: wline("#line "..g_lineno..' "'..g_fname..'"'). g_fname is the path dynasm was invoked with (dynasm.lua:945). vendor/luajit/build.zig:92 passes b.path(src ++ "vm_x64.dasc"), which Zig resolves to an ABSOLUTE Windows path using backslash separators. Backslashes are never escaped, so each path separator becomes a C escape sequence in the emitted string literal. Upstream never hits this because the MSVC build (msvcbuild.bat) invokes dynasm with a relative, single-component path.
impact: Latent, path-dependent build failure on Windows. A checkout at C:\...\2\R-Co\vendor\... survives only by accident: its sequences are \2 \R \v \s, and \v is a valid C escape while the rest are tolerated. A checkout at C:\...\2\rco-freshclone\vendor\... produces \r \c \v \s, and \c / \s / \l are invalid, so it fails with 77 errors. This means a genuine `git clone` into a directory whose name begins with an unlucky letter cannot build LuaJIT at all, while the maintainer's own checkout builds fine -- exactly the class of works-on-my-machine defect that hides in CI. Verified on a real `git clone` (not merely a worktree), where the path component \claude produced '\c' and \AppData produced '\A' and '\U used with no following hex digits'.
acceptance_criteria: dynasm-generated buildvm_arch.h contains #line directives whose path is a valid C string literal (backslashes escaped) on Windows.
`zig build test-lua` succeeds from a checkout whose absolute path contains sequences such as \c, \s, \l, \U, \A.
Behaviour on POSIX paths (no backslashes) is byte-for-byte unchanged.
resolution: vendor/luajit/dynasm/dynasm.lua:88 now escapes backslashes and double quotes in g_fname before interpolating it into the C string literal, via g_fname:gsub('[\\"]', '\\%0'). This is strictly correct C string-literal quoting and is a no-op for POSIX paths, which contain neither character. Fixed in the same run as ISS-0175 under the Unblock-Everything directive, because it blocked the fresh-clone verification that was ISS-0175's entire acceptance criterion.
verification: Before the fix, a real `git clone` into a path containing \claude\...\scratchpad failed with 'unknown escape sequence' / '\U used with no following hex digits' errors. After the fix, the same clone runs `zig build test-lua` to completion: 71/71 tests passed. The primary checkout also rebuilds clean (zig build, zig build test).
notes: Predicted but not confirmed by TEST-RUNNER during WF03-ISS-0169-20260806, and recorded as an unverified aside in the ISS-0175 notes field. This run confirmed it empirically and established that it is a REAL defect affecting genuine clones, not an artifact of `git worktree` as originally suspected. The distinguishing evidence: both the primary checkout and the failing worktree emit identically unescaped paths -- only the following letters differ, which is what decides success or failure.
